etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English wher, from Old English hwǣr (“where”, literally “at what place”), from Proto-Germanic *hwar (“where”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷo- (interrogative pronoun).

definitions.definition: In, at or to which place or situation.

quote.citation: 2013 July-August, Henry Petroski, “Geothermal Energy”, in American Scientist, volume 101, number 4:
quote.text: Energy has seldom been found where we need it when we want it. Ancient nomads, wishing to ward off the evening chill and enjoy a meal around a campfire, had to collect wood and then spend time and effort coaxing the heat of friction out from between sticks to kindle a flame. With more settled people, animals were harnessed to capstans or caged in treadmills to turn grist into meal.

quote.citation: 1967, Barbara Sleigh, Jessamy, Sevenoaks, Kent: Bloomsbury, published 1993, →ISBN, page 122:
quote.text: Through the open front door ran Jessamy, down the steps to where Kitto was sitting at the bottom with the pram beside him.

definitions.definition: In, at or to the place (that) or a place (that).
In, at or to any place (that); wherever; anywhere.
In a position, case, etc. in which; if.
While on the contrary; although; whereas.

quote.citation: 1595 December 9 (first known performance), William Shakespeare, “The life and death of King Richard the Second”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies: Published According to the True Originall Copies (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act III, scene ii]:
quote.text: And flight and die is death destroying death;  Where fearing dying pays death servile breath.

quote.citation: July 18 2012, Scott Tobias, AV Club The Dark Knight Rises[1]
quote.text: Where the Joker preys on our fears of random, irrational acts of terror, Bane has an all-consuming, dictatorial agenda that’s more stable and permanent, a New World Order that’s been planned out with the precision of a military coup.

quote.citation: 2013 June 14, Jonathan Freedland, “Obama's once hip brand is now tainted”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 1, page 18:
quote.text: Now we are liberal with our innermost secrets, spraying them into the public ether with a generosity our forebears could not have imagined. Where we once sent love letters in a sealed envelope, or stuck photographs of our children in a family album, now such private material is despatched to servers and clouds operated by people we don't know and will never meet.

definitions.definition: Interrogative adverb, used in either a direct or indirect question: in, at or to what place.
(fused relative) The place in, at or to which.
The place in which something happens.

quote.citation: 1590, Edmund Spenser, “Book III, Canto IV”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London:  […]  [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC, stanza 19:
quote.text: Finding the nymph a sleepe in secret wheare
